wins.text: Net income of $3.2B with EPS of $1.52 and RoTCE of 7.2%; total revenues up 4% YoY across all five core businesses
Investment banking fees up 63% YoY; Banking segment revenues up 38% driven by strong DCM, ECM and advisory activity with share gains across all three
Equities revenues up 37% YoY driven by strong derivatives performance including a gain on the Visa B exchange offer; prime balances up ~18%

Expenses down 2% YoY and 6% sequentially to $13.4B, generating positive operating leverage firm-wide; organizational simplification and stranded cost actions expected to drive $2B–$2.5B in annual run-rate saves over medium term

CET1 ratio at 13.6%, ~130 bps above current regulatory requirement; stress capital buffer reduced from 4.3% to 4.1%, lowering regulatory capital requirement to 12.1% as of October 1; dividend raised 6% to $0.56/share and $1B buyback planned for Q3

risks.text: Federal Reserve and OCC issued civil money penalties ($136M total) and an amended consent order requiring a new resource review plan; Citi acknowledged falling behind on data quality management related to regulatory reporting, with scope of remediation work expanded beyond original plan

USPB RoTCE of only 1.9% for Q2; cost of credit surged to $2.3B driven by $1.9B in NCLs and ~$400M ACL build; multiple card loan vintages maturing simultaneously compounding credit losses; Retail Services NCL rate guided to high end of 5.75%–6.25% range

Lower-income and lower-FICO consumers showing sharper drops in payment rates and increased borrowing; only the highest income quartile has more savings than pre-2019, creating bifurcated credit performance

NII ex-markets down ~3% sequentially, pressured by FX translation, seasonally lower revolving card balances, lower Argentina interest rates, and assumed higher deposit betas outside the U.S.; CFPB late fee rule impact still embedded in forecasts

Buyback guidance limited to quarterly determinations due to Basel III endgame uncertainty; intercompany dividends from CBNA to parent require OCC nonobjection until resource review plan is approved, adding near-term capital flexibility uncertainty

guidance_items.detail: Full-year 2024 expense guidance of $53.5B–$53.8B reaffirmed (excluding FDIC special assessment and $136M civil money penalty); management noted they will likely be at the higher end of the range
Full-year NII guided modestly down YoY; back half expected slightly higher than first half; medium-term targets unchanged
Branded cards NCL rate expected in 3.5%–4.0% range for full year; Retail Services at high end of 5.75%–6.25% range
Medium-term RoTCE target of 11%–12% reaffirmed; medium-term expense target of $51B–$53B for 2026 reaffirmed
$1B common share buyback planned for Q3 2024; dividend raised to $0.56/share as previously announced; future buybacks to be assessed quarterly

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Scope and timeline impact of the amended OCC consent order / resource review plan on capital flexibility and buyback pace
DTA utilization constraints and catalysts for accelerating NOL utilization beyond organic earnings
Competitive dynamics in Retail Services (co-brand cards) with peers leading on price to win new mandates
